notes: kb/Work PB1890 (landed, wave 1006 B) closes the one open exception docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-124 carried. cite.py --check 5.5 'the implementor shall define when the operand represents an integer' -> OK §5.5 3) a). The determination (an operand is an integer exactly when its value has no nonzero digit right of the point, tested on the exact value) now holds at every rule that asks: a fixed-point item at its declared scale (CobolNum.HasFraction via CobolTable.Occ / CobolString.RefModPosition), an expression or float subscript / ref-mod bound on its own carrier before any store (CobolTable.OccValue* / CobolString.RefModValue*, PB1890), a SET index or amount (CobolIndex), and an intrinsic integer argument (CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArg*, PB1526). The binary64 predicate is one function, CobolNum.HasFraction(double), shared by the intrinsic intake and the position intakes. GnuCOBOL offers no precedent (it truncates a subscript to int and never tests a fraction). Since kb/Work PB5886 the compile-time type 6 screen fails closed, so an accepted program reaches the intrinsic intake only with an integral value (or under --permissive); the intake's fraction test is witnessed by the unit test IntrinsicCarrierAgreementDriftTests, the position arm by the two PB1890 goldens and pb41_position_not_integer. retired-witness: conformance:cases/5.5-Integer-operands/pb1526_integer_argument_has_integral_value (kb/Work PB5886: the type 6 screen fails closed, so these programs' non-integral arguments are refused at compile time and no accepted program reaches the intrinsic intake with a fraction; the intake keeps its unit witness IntrinsicCarrierAgreementDriftTests) retired-witness: conformance:cases/5.5-Integer-operands/pb1526_integer_argument_integrality_standard_decimal (kb/Work PB5886: the type 6 screen fails closed, so these programs' non-integral arguments are refused at compile time and no accepted program reaches the intrinsic intake with a fraction; the intake keeps its unit witness IntrinsicCarrierAgreementDriftTests)
